notions.question: Why is an official report from 1942 regarded as the founding act of the British Welfare State?
notions.definition: Published in early December 1942, in the middle of the war, the report "Social Insurance and Allied Services" by the Liberal economist William Beveridge proposed a universal social security system to fight the "five giants": Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor and Idleness (that is, unemployment). It provided for a single national social insurance scheme financed by flat-rate contributions, giving entitlement to flat-rate benefits "from the cradle to the grave", and it assumed a national health service, family allowances and a policy of full employment. Hugely popular, it gave post-war reconstruction a programme.

termes.definition: A state that guarantees extensive social protection.
A protection scheme financed by contributions.

exemple.texte: The report, published in December 1942 under the title Social Insurance and Allied Services (Cmd. 6404), sold hundreds of thousands of copies and identified the "five giants" to be defeated.

confusions.explication: The report was the work of a Liberal under a coalition government; its implementation fell to Labour.

verification: Name the five "giants" of the Beveridge Report.

notions.titre: Attlee and the Welfare State: the NHS
notions.question: How did Labour build the Welfare State after 1945?
notions.definition: In July 1945, against all expectations, Clement Attlee's Labour Party heavily defeated Churchill's Conservatives. The Attlee government (1945-1951) implemented Beveridge's recommendations: the National Insurance Act (1946) and family allowances, the National Assistance Act (1948), and above all the National Health Service, created by the National Health Service Act 1946 and launched on 5 July 1948 under the leadership of the Minister of Health Aneurin Bevan: care free at the point of use, financed by taxation, for the whole population. To this were added nationalisations and a housebuilding policy. The Education Act 1944 (Butler), passed under the coalition, had already made free secondary education universal.

lignes: National Insurance Act; National Health Service Act

termes.definition: The British public health system, free at the point of use.

termes.en: free at the point of use
termes.es: gratuito en el punto de uso
termes.definition: No direct payment by the patient.

exemple.texte: The NHS was launched on 5 July 1948, following the National Health Service Act 1946 steered through by Aneurin Bevan.

verification: Who was behind the NHS and when was it launched?

notions.question: Which sectors did the British state take over after 1945, and why?
notions.definition: In line with Clause IV of the Labour Party constitution (common ownership of the means of production), the Attlee government nationalised the sectors regarded as strategic or failing: the Bank of England (1946), civil aviation (1946), coal (1947, National Coal Board), inland transport including the railways (1948), electricity (1948), gas (1949), then iron and steel (1951, denationalised by the Conservatives in 1953 and renationalised in 1967). Around a fifth of the economy came under public control. Aims: to modernise ageing industries, guarantee employment and plan reconstruction. These public corporations would be at the heart of debates on efficiency and decline, before the privatisations of the 1980s.

lignes: Iron and steel (denationalised in 1953, renationalised in 1967)

termes.definition: The transfer of a company to the public sector.
The coexistence of public and private sectors.
The article of the Labour constitution on common ownership, rewritten in 1995.

exemple.texte: A commentary on a 1947 poster proclaiming "Today the mines belong to the people" can be linked to the nationalisation of coal and to Clause IV.

confusions.explication: After privatisation, the state regulates rather than owns.

verification: Why does iron and steel illustrate the alternation of power in British politics?

questions.enonce: Which of these are "giants" identified by the Beveridge Report?

choix.explication: Not one of the five giants.

questions.enonce: Which minister is associated with the creation of the NHS?

choix.explication: Minister of Health in the Attlee government.
Author of the 1942 report, not a minister.

questions.enonce: On what ideological basis did Labour nationalise after 1945?

choix.texte: Clause IV of its constitution (common ownership of the means of production)

flashcards.question: Tell the story of the birth of the British Welfare State, from Beveridge to Attlee.
flashcards.reponse: 1942: Beveridge Report (Social Insurance and Allied Services) against the five giants (Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor, Idleness), universal protection "from the cradle to the grave". 1944: Education Act (Butler). July 1945: Labour victory under Attlee. 1946: National Insurance Act, NHS Act; 5 July 1948: launch of the NHS (Bevan), free and financed by taxation. Nationalisations: Bank of England (1946), coal (1947), rail and electricity (1948), gas (1949), steel (1951); a mixed economy in the name of Clause IV.
erreurs: Attributing the NHS to Beveridge or to Churchill
